General information.Name: Environmental impact of beef production in Mexico through life cycle assessment
General information.Category: Agricultura, Silvicultura, Pesca y Caza/112 Ganadería
General information.Description: Intensive and extensive systems of beef production in the Mexican tropics were analyzed. The aim of the study was to estimate and compare the environmental impact of two typical beef production systems in Veracruz, Mexico. A system boundary was established from farm production to prior to transport for consumer consumption, including intermediate stages of product processing, marketing and transportation. The functional unit was 1 kg of boneless and fatless beef. The life cycle inventory was built using information from case studies; farmers, slaughterhouses and retail point managers who provided information from records and expert knowledge were interviewed. The study included cow-calf processes, pre-fattening, fattening, processing and retail. Several impact categories were analyzed using SimaPro software and the ReCiPe Midpoint method for impact characterization. The results showed that for the extensive system, the cow-calf stage is the major contributor in eleven of the twelve impact categories analyzed, while in the intensive system, it is the main contributor to the climate change, terrestrial acidification, freshwater and marine eutrophication. The fattening stage of intensive system, has a predominant impact on human toxicity, water depletion, terrestrial ecotoxicity, fossil depletion, photo-oxidants formation, freshwater ecotoxicity and marine ecotoxicity; the processing stage has relevant contributions to fossil fuel depletion and the formation of photochemical oxidants in intensive systems. Finally, the marketing stage did not have a predominant impact on any category. The results indicated that the extensive system has better environmental performance than the intensive system for nine of the twelve studied categories.
General information.Tags: Life cycle assessment, Mexican beef, Extensive beef production, Intensive beef production, Mexican beef supply chain, Environmental impact assessment, Beef production in Mexican tropic
General information.Technology | Description: The analysis was performed using SimaPro 7.3.3 software for processing the inventory, ReCiPe Midpoint (H) method version 1.06. The ReCiPe method was selected because it is an actual and accepted method which uses mid and endpoint impact categories. It uses an environmental mechanism as a base for the impact model; similarly, it allows the quantification of the environmental impacts from specific indicators and was used to evaluate the twelve impact categories. These categories were: Climate change (CC in kg CO2 eq), Human Toxicity (HT in kg, 1.4-DB eq), Terrestrial Acidification (TA in kg, SO2 eq), Freshwater Eutrophication (FEU in kg Peq), Marine Eutrophication (MEU in kgNeq), Terrestrial Ecotoxicity (ET in kg 1,4-DB eq), Agricultural Land Occupation (ALO in m2 x yr), Water depletion (WD in m3), Fossil Depletion.

processDocumentation.LCI method: Life cycle assessment methodology according to ISO 14040:2006, using SimaPro 7.3.3 software and ReCiPe Midpoint (H) method version 1.06 for impact characterization
processDocumentation.Process type: Cradle-to-grave approach from farm production to prior to transport for consumer consumption, including intermediate stages of product processing, marketing and transportation
processDocumentation.Modeling constants: Tier 1 methodology of IPCC (2006) for methane emissions from cattle enteric fermentation and manure; direct and indirect nitrous oxide and ammonia manure emissions; economic allocation (64.5% to milk and 35.5% to calf production) for cow-calf stage; functional unit: 1 kg of boneless and fatless beef
processDocumentation.Data source information: 17 case studies via interviews with farmers, slaughterhouse representatives and marketing point sellers; supplemented by literature values and expert interviews; data from Mexican government entities (FIRA, INEGI, SAGARPA, SEMARNAT)
processDocumentation.Data completeness: Comprehensive coverage of all major processes: cow-calf, pre-fattening, fattening, processing and marketing stages; includes animals, pasture, concentrates, fertilizers, pesticides, water, electricity, gas, packaging, transportation, organic waste disposal
processDocumentation.Data selection: Included: all material and energy flows relevant to beef production chain; Excluded: infrastructure and equipment according to LCA best practices (European Commission, 2010)
processDocumentation.Data treatment: Data validation through consultations with livestock associations, researchers, academics and extension specialists; comparison with published data, reports and domestic statistics
processDocumentation.Sampling procedure: Purposive sampling of representative case studies: 2 ranches for cow-calf process; 2 case studies per process and system for pre-fattening, fattening and processing stages; convenience sampling for marketing points (supermarket chain for IS, butcher houses for ES)
processDocumentation.Data collection period: One year of operations for each livestock production, processing and marketing unit analyzed; specific collection dates not specified
processDocumentation.Use advice: Results specific to Mexican tropical conditions in Veracruz; applicable to similar dual-purpose and feedlot systems; limitations in generalizability to other regions with different production conditions
processDocumentation.Completeness: High completeness with comprehensive system boundaries covering entire production chain; data validated through multiple sources and expert consultation
processDocumentation.Sources: ANETIF, 2011; CEPAL-FAO-ICA, 2013; FIRA, 2012; FAO, 2010; INEGI, 2007; SIAP, 2011; Signorini et al., 2006; IPCC, 2006; European Commission, 2010
processDocumentation.Project: Knowledge-based Sustainable vAlue-added food chains: innovative tools for monitoring ethical, environmental and Socio-economical impActs and implementing Eu-Latin America shared strategies, Grant agreement no.: 265927, Seventh Framework Program
processDocumentation.Intended application: Quantification and comparison of environmental impacts of intensive and extensive beef production systems in Mexico; identification of hotspots along beef value chains; recommendations for sustainable production improvements
processDocumentation.Data set owner: Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México, Facultad de Medicina Veterinaria y Zootecnia and Instituto de Ingeniería
processDocumentation.Data set generator: Adriana Rivera Huerta, Leonor Patricia Güereca, María de la Salud Rubio Lozano
processDocumentation.Data set documentor: Adriana Rivera Huerta, Leonor Patricia Güereca, María de la Salud Rubio Lozano
processDocumentation.Access and use restrictions: Standard Elsevier copyright restrictions apply; supplementary data available online at http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.resconrec.2016.01.020
